findings.text: The test 'skips patterns with an empty body' doesn't test what it claims. Without the `body === ''` guard (src/ignore.ts:30), `/`, `!` and `!/` compile to `(?:^|/)$`, which no non-empty path matches. So `ignored('a.ts', false)` is false either way, and the test passes with the guard removed.

The goal's command part, `--no-ignore`, has no test. Nothing runs the command with or without the flag, so a regression there (for example, dropping `{ ignore }` at cli.ts:12) would not be caught. Only `scanFolder`'s option is covered.

Only ENOENT counts as 'no .locignore'. If `<root>/.locignore` is a folder (EISDIR), or can't be read (EACCES), `ignoreMatcher` throws. `scanFolder` and the `loc` command then fail with an unhandled rejection and stack trace, not the command's `loc: ...` error and exit code 2. A `.locignore` folder should probably count as no ignore file.

`?` compiles to `[^/]` in a RegExp without the `u` flag (line 31), so it matches one UTF-16 code unit, not one character. A character outside the BMP is two code units, so `?.ts` does not match `😀.ts`, and `??.ts` does. The goal says `?` matches one character. Fix: add the `u` flag, which the escaping already supports.

A UTF-8 BOM is not stripped. In a `.locignore` saved with a BOM, the first pattern becomes `﻿<pattern>` and never matches. If the first line is a `#` comment, it is no longer skipped (harmless, but wrong). Git strips the BOM, so the first pattern line is silently ignored here.

blind.summary: The change meets the goal. I found no blocker or major defects after tracing the patterns in the goal (`*.log`, `build`, `/dist`, `src/gen`, `out/`, `**/x`, `x/**`, `a/**/b`, `!` with last-match-wins, and no re-including under an ignored folder) through `globToRegex`, `parse` and the prefix loop. `ignoreMatcher` is exported. `scanFolder` skips ignored files and folders, still counts `.locignore`, and accepts `{ ignore: false }`. The command takes `--no-ignore`. `tsconfig` targets ES2023, so `findLast` typechecks. I read the code but did not run `npm run check`. What's left is minor: one test passes even with the code it tests removed, `--no-ignore` has no test, and three edge cases in reading the file and matching names.
